findings.reason: without a node owning the persist-layer abort, the rerun stops at the same guard on every attempt and §51's done-when ("every source in the rerun cohort reads back as produced, or failed with a reason written by this rerun") cannot be reached; the section's node list is incomplete for its own goal.
findings.text: §51 reasons about §50's run only and declares no node for the defect that stopped the rerun §51 exists to finish: `sib-second-pass` ran as SLURM job 1308283 (run 9192044a, recorded in this same document's s50 comment `c-run-r-20261108T051738232687-sib-second-pass`) and ended EXIT=1 with `stop_reason: failed` on `RuntimeError: rich standard-name write rejected an exact-claim winner` raised from `persist_generated_name_winners`, "which aborts the batch" (23 of the pool's errors), a persist-layer refusal that is never recorded against a source; the only trace of it in the plan is that one §50 comment, while §51's five nodes (reset, drained-exit, refusal-narrowing, spelling-retry, receipts) close none of it, so a node dispatched from §51 reruns the cohort into the same abort

— §51's measure and its ceiling cannot both hold, so the section's mechanism cannot produce its done-when: it states "the rerun cohort's ceiling is 114 new identities with none guaranteed" beside "spend is at most USD 50" and "at least 3 accepted new names per USD spent", and 114 / 3 = USD 38, so any spend between USD 38 and the authorised USD 50 fails the rate floor even at the cohort's maximum possible yield — the recorded rerun spent USD 1.4855 for 20 accepted (about 13.5 per USD), so the rate is met only while the cohort's yield, not its arithmetic, is what binds; WOULD_CHANGE_THE_PLAN: yes — REASON: a node can be judged failed for spending its authorised budget while delivering at the cohort's ceiling, so either the USD 50 cap or the 3-per-USD floor must be restated against the 114 ceiling.

— the second done-when bullet binds negative controls to "each defect node", which reaches three of the five declared nodes: `sib-second-pass` (the node that carries the cohort measure, with no regression test declared and no control) and `sib-claim-outcome-receipts` (a new writer on the compose batch failure path, dispatched after `sib-compose-refusal-narrowing`) name no test and no declared negative control, so their guards cannot be shown to fire; WOULD_CHANGE_THE_PLAN: yes — REASON: the section's closing verdict would accept two nodes on a read-back alone, and the receipts writer in particular is exactly the kind of untested write path the rest of the plan gates with a failing-then-passing test.

— the `_document` declaration marks `s50: done` while §50's own text records the opposite: "Accepted names rose … That is 4.1 accepted per USD, but under the section's own 500 bar, and the cap did not stop the run, so the yield clause is not met", and §50's done-when itself says "A lower yield is a defect to diagnose, not a pass"; §50 also never mentions §51 as its successor, so a reader of the declarations sees a section closed whose own measure was missed; WOULD_CHANGE_THE_PLAN: yes — REASON: the remainder is now carried by §51, but the declarations alone hide that §50's bar was missed, and a coordinator dispatching from section state will read §50's bar as met.

— §51's done-when requires a per-source read-back, spend by the run's own id, and the export gate's blocking set read "with the gate's own predicate", and names no path for any of them, where §50 named `~/.cache/imas-codex-full-dd-run/` for its job log; WOULD_CHANGE_THE_PLAN: no — REASON: the nodes already write evidence fragments under `docs/evidence/fragments/sn-integrity-backlog/`, so the omission costs a line of clarity rather than directing work to a lost path.

— the quantitative basis of the section, "the rerun cohort's ceiling is 114 new identities with none guaranteed", carries no citation, while the diagnosis it rests on (`sib-full-run-failure-diagnosis`, merge `a0a536030`) records the 114 unproduced cohort in its fragment; a reader cannot tell which measurement or commit fixes the 114, and the whole decision to measure yield per USD instead of a name count rests on it; WOULD_CHANGE_THE_PLAN: no — REASON: the figure is corroborated by the cited diagnosis, so a citation belongs in the sentence but the section's direction would not change.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — the "114 new identities" ceiling has no anchor; the diagnosis merge and every section href resolve, and extensionless targets resolve as `<path>.html`.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — two of §51's five nodes fall outside the done-when's "each defect node's regression test" clause, and the `_document` declaration `s50: done` contradicts §51's own statement that §50's yield clause was not met.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: a finding — §51 names no durable path for the cohort read-back, the spend ledger or the export-gate reading, where §50 supplied `~/.cache/imas-codex-full-dd-run/` for its log.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the section and its symbols carry no ticket numbers, stage labels or version tags, and the prose states the mechanism (spelling refusal, queue drain, refusal narrowing) rather than citing tracker entries.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §51 declares no node for the persist guard that stopped its own rerun, and its per-USD yield floor is arithmetically unreachable against its own stated ceiling at the authorised spend.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each of the five nodes names one deliverable, and the catalog-consistency pass that was a second, unmeasured goal in §50 is now explicitly "its own node" outside this section.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §51 links `sn-integrity-backlog#s50` (the section whose work it continues), and the one external artefact it relies on, `sib-full-run-failure-diagnosis` merge `a0a536030`, resolves in the tree; each of the five node ids is declared in the section's own prose and `sib-claim-outcome-receipts` carries its ordering against `sib-compose-refusal-narrowing` in text.
